pilot_gt21.summary: The GT21 pilot reproduces and is done; this is not scientific approval. My own adapter, on fresh subjects (AB10, AB13), labelled tasks from the heel path, assigned plates per contact segment, and covered treadmill, overground, incline, decline, stair ascent and stair descent. It found 0 wrong signs applied or suggested in 216 leg-channels, and all 187 single-test votes were right. The worker's 648 leg-channels recount exactly. The ground truth matches GT21-C01. Pelvis-rise task labels cannot flip a sign. Both detector fixes are correct, and from stored evidence they cannot have changed any UM21, GT23 or GT24 verdict. The 'off-grid' AB24 recording is a plate file that starts 1 ms after the kinematics, not an off-grid clock. The sheet meets the rules. Recommendations are not blocking.

checks.name: Latest-round rule (temp backlog and verify files; real files untouched)
cases: Newest round has no timestamp (round_2 back_to_worker): it sorts as '' (oldest), so verified_done is True. Hole.
Equal timestamps, done round listed first: True. With the back round listed first: False. Result depends on order.
Newer round with a naive timestamp '2026-10-31T10:00:00' (back) against '09:00:00Z' (done): False, correct here only because the strings happen to sort.
Newer round with an offset '2026-10-31T05:30:00-05:00' (10:30Z, back) against '09:00:00Z' (done): True. Hole, because strings are compared, not times.
Newer round with a space separator '2026-10-31 10:00:00Z' (back): True. Hole, because ' ' sorts before 'T'.
Rounds kept in a list (rounds: [...]) with a later back_to_worker: True. Hole, because only top-level dicts are seen.
checks.ruling: List or key order should not decide either. Repository conventions differ: some verify files prepend new rounds (CORE-04-verify), others append (round_1, round_2), and key names vary ('pilot_gt24_round_3', 'rule_b_switch'). Fail closed instead. A refutation is verified only if the top-level verdict is done and every round-like record (dicts and list items carrying a verdict) has a timezone-aware ISO timestamp, parsed as a datetime. The newest round must be unique and done. Any missing, naive or unparseable timestamp, or a tie involving a non-done round, makes it not verified, and the statement is kept with the reason logged.

checks.ruling: Match a citation key exactly, or at least require the locator to start the citation and be followed by a non-alphanumeric character or the end of the string. The adapter's citation must name the document. Do not use a free substring.

The frame can still be wrong, but CoP progression tests it: heel-to-toe in every leg. Without heel and toe markers the CoP-within-foot check is unknown, so the lever arm stays moderate.

module_checks.evidence: Under rule B the named directions are hip flexion, knee flexion and ankle dorsiflexion. With the person facing +x and z = the person's right, hip flexion (knee forward) and dorsiflexion (toes up) are counterclockwise, while knee flexion (shank swings back) is clockwise. So only the knee factor is -1. Segment angles stay counterclockwise (pelvis anterior tilt negative).

marker_reference_angles gives joint = JOINT_CCW x (distal - proximal), so knee = -(shank - thigh). A thigh vertical with the ankle 0.2 m behind the knee gives +0.47 rad; my test asserts > 0.3. For a planar leg, the knee equals thigh - shank to 1e-15.

With target = s x source, s_d d = s_q q - s_j j, so the fitted b = -s_d s_j and the relation product is c x b with c = -1. A source built as shank = thigh - knee gives product +1 for (shank, knee); a rule-C-built shank gives -1. Pattern votes come from source data before c is applied, so they do not change between rules.

lever = -JOINT_CCW x (r x F)_z = +(r x F)_z for the knee. GRF behind the knee gives an internal extensor moment, which is counterclockwise on the shank and so negative under rule B. My test builds the truth with numpy's 3D cross product and recovers +1 and -1 for flipped sources through lever_arm_test('knee').
A large excursion on the positive side now votes +1 (flexion positive already), the mirror of rule C. Thresholds are unchanged and symmetric in sign.

The ankle and hip lever arms, the late-stance plantarflexor test, the power identity (both knee moment and knee angle flip, so the product is invariant), the plate frame checks, the branch screen and the vertical order do not depend on the knee convention.

round_1.summary: The rule-C physics is right, the vote, bootstrap and flag rules are fixed in advance, deterministic and implemented as written, and no code path applies an offset or applies a sign from documentation or a template alone. Four defects send it back. (1) In a force-plate frame whose forward axis is reversed, the ankle lever arm alone applies the wrong moment sign whenever the late-stance test abstains (task=None, which the design asks for in atypical populations). The design note's claim that the marker angles catch this is not implemented. (2) One-hop propagation can derive a sign from a channel that another relation has already put in conflict. (3) An inverted up vector mirrors every marker reference angle with no check, so every marker-anchored channel would apply the wrong sign. (4) A channel stored with 360-degree wraps gets a flagged offset of exactly 2*pi. Each defect has a strict-xfail test in tests/test_sign_offset_detector_verify.py. No research data was read.

checks.name: Physics under rule C
checks.result: pass (with fix 3 on an input precondition)
checks.evidence: I derived the rules myself with x forward, y up and z = x cross y = the person's right. The internal moment on the distal segment from static equilibrium about the joint is M = -(r x F)_z, r = CoP - joint, F = GRF on the body. Code line 329 equals this, and I checked it against numpy's 3D cross product. CoP ahead of the ankle under upward GRF gives a negative (plantarflexor) internal moment. GRF behind the knee gives a positive (extensor) moment. Both match the rule table. lever_arm_test recovers both source signs. Segment chain: thigh measured from straight down (distal forward +), foot heel->toe from horizontal (toes up +), pelvis PSIS->ASIS from horizontal (anterior tilt -). Joint = distal - proximal therefore gives hip flexion +, knee flexion - and ankle dorsiflexion +. My labelled postures confirm all four (knee 0.2 m ahead, ankle behind the knee, toe above heel, ASIS below PSIS). Power: M*dq/dt is positive at push-off (plantarflexing velocity with plantarflexor moment). power_relation returns product -1 for -(M*w) storage and +1 for M*w with dt=None. Projection: across 8 random headings, each with a random lateral reflection, the angles equal the planar truth to 1e-9. It uses only dot products, so lab handedness does not matter. It does depend on the sign of the 'up' input. With up inverted, every marker angle is mirrored (knee r = -0.9997 vs truth), and nothing checks for this (fix 3).

checks.name: Safety paths
checks.evidence: Offsets: _bootstrap_offset always sets applied=False. apply_signs only multiplies channels with sign_applied. My test confirms a +0.1 rad offset survives in the output byte for byte. Documentation and template evidence score 0. Documentation alone, template alone, and documentation plus an agreeing template all give abstain. A moderate or strong dissent gives conflict; a weak dissent still gives apply/medium, as designed. Defect A (fix 1): with the plate frame mirrored forward, verdicts are level_walking -> conflict (the late-stance test dissents, correct) but task=None -> apply -1, which is wrong. A single strong lever-arm vote reaches score 2 and depends entirely on a frame the detector does not check. Design note sentence 'The marker-angle test catches this, because the knee and ankle must agree' has no implementation: no test links angle or marker evidence to moment channels. Origin mismatch between CoP and joints of 0.3 or 0.6 m gave abstain or the correct sign in my probes, so this case is less acute. Defect B (fix 2): _propagate snapshots 'direct' before the loop. A channel turned to conflict by a contradicting relation therefore still counts as applied for later relations. Demonstrated: a faulty hip reference puts thigh and hip in conflict, yet shank_angle gets apply from derived:segment_chain off the conflicted thigh. Circularity otherwise: derived evidence is never used to derive further, because of the pre-loop snapshot. Power cannot be applied directly, so a moment cannot be derived from a power anchor. Independent-segment references built from the same IK angles remain circular, which the design note discloses.

checks.name: Statistical rules and failure modes
checks.result: pass on rules; fail on wrap/offset interaction (fix 4); recommendations on other failure modes
checks.evidence: DEFAULTS are fixed constants, echoed into every report. My parametrised vote tests give: 4 units abstain; 5 units decide; 9/10 decide (both signs); 8/10 abstain. Offset: the median of per-unit medians, from agreeing units only. The 95% percentile bootstrap uses seed 20261030 with 2000 resamples and is identical on repeat. The CI contains injected offsets of +-0.06 and 0.02 rad. Its width falls within 0.5-1.6x the asymptotic median CI 2*1.96*1.2533*sigma/sqrt(n). The flag is set for +-0.06 and not for 0.02 rad, even though that CI excludes 0. Defect C (fix 4): an angle stored on [0, 2*pi) with about half its frames wrapped gets estimate 2*pi, CI [2*pi, 2*pi] and flag_for_review=True. The screen masked the other half of the frames as 'wrap_360'. Non-blocking observations: (a) Degrees passed through detect_leg: the branch screen masked about 3300 of 3600 frames. Hip abstained, and knee was still applied (medium) on the remaining frames with scale_review=True. The sign was correct, but the units are evidently wrong. (b) Deep knee flexion of 125 degrees (squat or sit-to-stand) is masked and counted as 'branch_180_frames'. (c) stance_from_grf is relative to each unit's peak, so a contact-free unit with 2 N noise is 88% 'stance'. (d) Out-and-back passes with one forward axis: units on the return pass are mirrored and the test abstains (12/24). This is safe, but the forward axis should be per pass. (e) Left/right: projection and lever arm use only [forward, up], and detection runs per leg, so the left leg is viewed from the right under rule C with no mirroring hazard inside the detector. (f) Treadmill vs overground: CoP and joint centres must share origin and axes; this is the caller's job and is covered by fix 1. (g) If the pelvis excursion is near noise, the chain fit abstains on both pairs, including the well-determined distal/joint pair. This is conservative.

Note: the worker's fixtures build their moment truth with the same lever formula as the module, and their chain truth with the same CHAIN sums.
